editorial:
Imagine having every powerful person in town as your best friend, but only because you pay for everything. That is exactly how you start with Timon. He is a rich guy who loves throwing the biggest parties in Athens, spending his money like it is water just to be liked. The vibe is high-energy and flashy at first, making you feel the rush of his wild lifestyle. You get to see how easy it is to be popular when you are footing the bill for everyone else, but you can also tell that these friendships are fake and built on greed.

What really hits hard is how fast everything falls apart. The acting is top-notch, making the shift from a fancy party to a lonely cave feel real. The pacing is steady, though some of the old-school dialogue might take a minute to get used to. If you enjoy stories about betrayal and revenge, you should definitely check this out. It looks great if you can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, but picking up the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection is the best way to catch all the stage details.
endingExplained: After losing everything, Timon lives in a cave and hates everyone. He finds gold in the dirt, but instead of using it to get rich again, he uses it to tempt people into being greedy. In the end, Timon realizes that humans are just too selfish to ever change. He dies alone and bitter, leaving his gold behind. It is a sad ending that shows how hate and loneliness can eat a person alive.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about betrayal and the dark side of wealth.
